newsitem.title: USA: Peru's Fujimori optimistic for talks with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori optimistic for talks with rebels.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said on Sunday he was optimistic for a start to formal talks with rebels in the hostage crisis due to the possibility of the guerrillas giving some ground on their main demand.

While Fujimori did not say the rebels would reduce their demands for the release of their jailed comrades, he told the CNN International television network he hoped they would not directly refer to it in a forthcoming statement being worked out with the government.
"In the coming document of the (Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement) MRTA we may read it is not written expressly the liberation of MRTA prisoners," Fujimori said in English.

All recent statements by the MRTA have expressly called for talks to include their demand for the release of about 400 jailed comrades in return for their 72 hostages. Fujimori said in Toronto on Saturday he planned to resume talks, which have been on hold for weeks because the government refuses to discuss the demand.
Fujimori added the government had been holding informal talks with the rebels through the visits of Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani to the besieged Japanese ambassador's home.

"We have advanced, in fact, for beginning this preliminary dialogue. We have advanced in such a way that some bases have already been established," Fujimori said. He expected "some advance" to be made on the document "in the next days."
